topic: Ottawa rules and radiograph request appropriateness
usual_baseline: Roughly half of requests comply. Overall compliance was 59.5% [1459], with ankle as low as 33.1% [1459] and 43% [1492]. Knee compliance was 72.5% [1519], but at least one knee rule was documented in only 41% [1499]. The ankle rules were referenced in 37% of requests [1520]. Of GP knee radiographs, 50% were within RCR guidelines [1574].
fix_that_works: Teaching, posters, leaflets and emails: overall 59.5% to 85% and ankle 33.1% to 75.8% [1459]; knee documentation 41% to 91% (p<0.01) [1499]. Handout plus teaching: ankle requests 43% to 57% and foot 32% to 54% [1492]. Governance presentation with radiographer briefings: 37% to 51% [1520].
fix_that_fails: Knee compliance rose from 72.5% to 83.5%, which was not significant (p=0.15) and still below the 95% target [1519]. Telling GPs the results left knee radiograph referral rates unchanged [1574]. Several audits stayed below target after education [1519, 1520].
consultant_advice: Ottawa rules audits are very common, and education reliably gives a short-term rise. That makes them low in novelty. More useful measures are sustained compliance after junior doctors rotate, the X-ray fracture yield, and whether an electronic request prompt holds the gains.
